editorial_thesis: The strongest fresh signal is operational: agents need observable oversight, portable developer surfaces, and explicit boundaries for people affected by their actions.

topic_groups.title: Agent Oversight + Security Operations
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Fresh operational controls are shifting agent security from prompt testing to inventory, anomaly detection, runtime evidence, and policy response.

sources.title: Agent Anomaly Detection
sources.why_selected: Use the pattern for a Buildn job monitor: statistical pass, targeted reasoning review, then policy callback.
sources.usefulness: Prototype a session-risk event schema with severity, evidence, and recommended action.

sources.title: Cisco AI Defense release line
sources.why_selected: Borrow the inventory → profile → runtime-event loop for client agent reviews.
sources.usefulness: Map one client workflow into assets, tools, identities, events, and response owners.

sources.title: Muse Secure VM
sources.why_selected: Use the isolated-worker and approval-receipt ideas for high-impact Buildn automations.
sources.usefulness: Write a threat model for an agent that browses, remembers, and transacts.

sources.title: JetBrains managed sandbox controls
sources.why_selected: Turn sandbox posture into a standard client discovery question, not an IDE afterthought.
sources.usefulness: Create a least-privilege sandbox checklist for agent-enabled developer environments.

sources.title: OWASP-aligned anomaly categories
sources.why_selected: Use the categories as a compact red-team taxonomy for Buildn client pilots.
sources.usefulness: Select one measurable detector per category and add it to a pilot scorecard.

topic_groups.title: Portable Agent Developer Surfaces
topic_groups.selection_rationale: The practical portability gap is narrowing: SDK generation, model routing, scheduled tasks, and BYOK are becoming explicit interfaces that can be tested and swapped.

sources.title: OpenAPI generation in the open
sources.why_selected: Generate stable client surfaces and live schema access for Buildn workers instead of hand-maintained wrappers.
sources.usefulness: Run the generator against one small Buildn-owned OpenAPI spec and compare maintenance cost.

sources.title: HydraFusion model orchestration
sources.why_selected: Use semantic routing as a reference for evidence extraction: cheap pass first, escalate ambiguity.
sources.usefulness: Define three task classes and benchmark routing against a fixed model baseline.

sources.title: Visual Studio BYOK Agent preview
sources.why_selected: Offer client-sensitive experiments with approved endpoints while preserving one task contract.
sources.usefulness: Document a provider-neutral agent task contract with model, tools, and evidence fields.

sources.title: Recurring agent tasks in VS Code
sources.why_selected: Translate recurring research and health checks into reviewable scheduled artifacts.
sources.usefulness: Design a recurring-job envelope: trigger, scope, evidence, approval, rollback.

sources.title: Documentation MCP generation
sources.why_selected: Keep agent tool knowledge synchronized with source specs, reducing guessed method names.
sources.usefulness: Add schema freshness and source commit to every tool manifest.

topic_groups.title: Human–Agent Boundaries
topic_groups.selection_rationale: New HCI work is filling a neglected gap: agents affect non-users, relationships, memory, and recovery, so adoption depends on calibrated control rather than raw autonomy.

sources.title: Design Principles for Human-Agent Interaction
sources.why_selected: Turn the principles into a Buildn review rubric for transparency, initiative, memory, and recovery.
sources.usefulness: Score one existing workflow against the 14 principles and log the largest gaps.

sources.title: When assistants involve others
sources.why_selected: Use the non-user lens for client workflows involving shared inboxes, meetings, documents, or delegated messages.
sources.usefulness: Add a non-user impact section to every agent opportunity brief.

sources.title: Calibrated expectations
sources.why_selected: Make the first-run experience state what the agent may do, cannot do, and when it asks.
sources.usefulness: Write a 60-second onboarding script plus a recovery example for one agent.

sources.title: Memory as a relationship contract
sources.why_selected: Separate durable user-approved facts from transient run context in Buildn artifacts.
sources.usefulness: Define memory classes, retention, review, deletion, and provenance fields.

sources.title: Repair is part of the product
sources.why_selected: Design human checkpoints with a clear explanation, reversible alternative, and next-best action.
sources.usefulness: Add failure receipts and rollback links to the next agent prototype.
